core_obligations: Construct S (proof lines 7706-7715): choose a surjection from a polynomial ring over R onto l with kernel a maximal ideal m, and let S be the m-adic completion of that polynomial ring; then S is an object of the category over l and R -> S is formally smooth in the adic topology because the polynomial ring is formally smooth over R and formal smoothness is stable under completion.

Reduce to constructing a smooth morphism (proof lines 7717-7731): since xi is versal its transformation is smooth, and by the change of residue field lemma the induced transformation is smooth, so it suffices to construct a smooth morphism from the functor of S to the changed functor of R.

Construct the morphism and check smoothness (proof lines 7731-7751): such a morphism assigns to a map S -> B the composition R -> S -> B, whose image lies in the subalgebra of B cut out by l; given a surjection B' -> B and a compatible diagram, the required ring map S -> B' exists exactly by the formal smoothness of R -> S in the adic topology, which gives a versal formal object of the changed functor lying over S.
proof_roadmap: Build the ring S as an adic completion of a polynomial ring over R and check the category and formal smoothness properties.
Use the smoothness of the versal transformation and its stability under change of residue field to reduce to a smoothness statement.
Verify the lifting property of the morphism on functors through the formal smoothness of R -> S.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a versal formal object over R of a deformation situation can be transported to the changed residue field: there are a ring S in the category over the larger residue field with R -> S formally smooth in the adic topology inducing the field extension, and a versal formal object of the changed functor lying over S (statement lines 7692-7704). The proof (proof lines 7706-7753) constructs S as an adic completion of a polynomial ring over R, reduces to a smoothness statement using the stability of smoothness under change of residue field, and verifies the lifting property through formal smoothness. H2: a three-step construction with three inputs, written out in full.
